name: DAX: filter context, time intelligence and iterators

refs.title: Use variables to improve your DAX formulas

steps: Write and put side by side in a table by Category with a Region slicer set to West: [Net Sales], CALCULATE([Net Sales], ALL(DimProduct)), CALCULATE([Net Sales], ALLSELECTED(DimProduct)), CALCULATE([Net Sales], ALLEXCEPT(DimProduct, DimProduct[Category])), CALCULATE([Net Sales], REMOVEFILTERS()), CALCULATE([Net Sales], KEEPFILTERS(DimProduct[Category] = "Water")).
Now add a visual-level filter Category ≠ Apparel and watch which columns change.
Write a one-line comment above each measure describing which filters it keeps.
asg.exp: ALL ignores the visual filter; ALLSELECTED respects it. KEEPFILTERS gives blank on non-Water rows instead of the Water number.

steps: Extend FactSales mentally: it only spans Jan–Mar 2026, so YoY will be blank. That is fine; you are testing the pattern, not the data.

Write: Sales MTD = TOTALMTD([Net Sales], Dates[Date]), Sales QTD, Sales PM = CALCULATE([Net Sales], DATEADD(Dates[Date], -1, MONTH)), MoM % = DIVIDE([Net Sales] - [Sales PM], [Sales PM]), Sales Rolling 30 = CALCULATE([Net Sales], DATESINPERIOD(Dates[Date], MAX(Dates[Date]), -30, DAY)).
Line chart by Date with Net Sales and Sales Rolling 30.
Break it: remove the "mark as date table" flag and observe what happens to Sales PM. Restore it.
asg.exp: Feb MoM % is computed. Sales PM for January is blank. Rolling 30 is smooth. Unmarking the date table does not break these measures because you referenced Dates[Date] directly; then delete the relationship and watch them break.

steps: Write Avg Sales per Customer = AVERAGEX(VALUES(DimCustomer[CustomerKey]), [Net Sales]) and compare to DIVIDE([Net Sales], [Customers Buying]).

Write Best Product Sales = MAXX(VALUES(DimProduct[ProductName]), [Net Sales]) and Best Product = the name, using TOPN(1, VALUES(DimProduct[ProductName]), [Net Sales]) wrapped in MAXX to return a text.
Write Customer Rank = RANKX(ALL(DimCustomer[CustomerName]), [Net Sales], , DESC, DENSE). Put it in a table by CustomerName. Then make it respect the slicer by swapping ALL for ALLSELECTED.
asg.exp: Rank 1 customer is unique. Customers Over 500 total is not the sum across regions (a customer can appear in two regions if reps cross regions).

steps: Rewrite MoM % with VAR cur, VAR prev, VAR delta and RETURN. Add a temporary RETURN prev to inspect the intermediate value, then restore.
Write a measure that returns a text: "Net " & FORMAT([Net Sales], "$#,##0") & " across " & [Orders] & " orders". Put it in a card.
Install DAX Studio, connect to your open PBIX, and run: EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS(DimProduct[Category], "Sales", [Net Sales]). Then turn on Server Timings and note the SE vs FE split.
asg.exp: You can state the FE and SE milliseconds for one query.

steps: Budget = SUM(FactBudget[BudgetAmount]). Variance = [Net Sales] - [Budget]. Variance % = DIVIDE([Variance], [Budget]).
Attainment Status = SWITCH(TRUE(), ISBLANK([Budget]), "No budget", [Variance %] >= 0, "On target", [Variance %] >= -0.1, "Watch", "Behind").
Use Attainment Status for conditional formatting (field value) on a matrix.
asg.exp: Product-level rows show "No budget" because budget is only at category grain.

int.q: ALL vs ALLSELECTED vs REMOVEFILTERS: one sentence each.
int.a: ALL removes filters from the given table/columns. REMOVEFILTERS is ALL restricted to being a CALCULATE modifier (clearer intent, cannot be used as a table). ALLSELECTED restores the filters from outside the visual (slicers) while removing the visual's own row/column filters.

int.q: Why does a measure inside SUMX need CALCULATE, and why don't you write it?
int.a: Row context does not filter. A measure reference is implicitly wrapped in CALCULATE (context transition), which turns the current row into a filter. That is why AVERAGEX(VALUES(Customer), [Net Sales]) works; writing SUM(FactSales[...]) inside would ignore the row.

int.q: What does DATEADD do when the previous period has no data, and how does that differ from SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR?
int.a: DATEADD returns the set of shifted dates that exist in the date table; if the fact has no rows the measure is blank. SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is DATEADD(-1, YEAR). Both require a proper date table. PARALLELPERIOD returns whole periods instead of the same dates.

The second argument is evaluated in the current filter context, so every row ranks against itself. Use ALL/ALLSELECTED on the column being ranked, and make sure the expression is a measure (context transition) not a raw column.

int.q: What is the difference between VALUES and DISTINCT?
int.a: VALUES includes the blank row created by referential-integrity violations; DISTINCT does not. In iterators over dimension keys the difference can move a total.

int.q: Explain context transition and one case where it hurts performance.
int.a: When a measure (or CALCULATE) is evaluated in row context, the row values become filters. Inside SUMX over a 10-million-row fact, calling a measure per row causes 10 million context transitions and a huge formula-engine cost; rewrite with column arithmetic or pre-aggregated tables.

ass.q: CALCULATE([Net Sales], ALLSELECTED(DimProduct)) in a table by Category with a visual filter Category ≠ Apparel and slicer Region = West shows:
o: West total excluding Apparel, on every row
ass.why: ALLSELECTED keeps slicer and visual filters but removes the row's category.
